description: Verified exam notes for 6 November 2026 covering semiconductor policy, rice-market intervention, digital public services, telecom regulation, highways, cancer-drug pricing, research infrastructure and livestock biosecurity.

stories.title: Semicon 2.0 portal opens applications and 12 new ECMS projects are approved
stories.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology launched the Semicon 2.0 web application portal on 6 November and opened applications for three pillars covering machines and materials, additional fabrication facilities, and stronger ATMP/OSAT capacity. It also announced 12 approved applications under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme. These are approvals and projected outcomes, not completed production or employment.
key_facts: The Union Cabinet-approved fiscal outlay for Semicon 2.0 is ₹1,27,500 crore.
Applications are live for Pillar 2 (Machines and Materials), Pillar 3 (More Fabs) and Pillar 4 (ATMP/OSAT strengthening).
The 12 ECMS approvals project ₹7,503 crore of investment, ₹39,045 crore of production and 7,127 direct jobs.
Approved projects span seven states, including Tamil Nadu; the Tamil Nadu-linked approvals include relays and precision moulds and tooling.
Across all ECMS approvals announced so far, 118 applications covering 34 products in 16 states project ₹77,051 crore of investment.
stories.exam_link: Revise the India Semiconductor Mission, semiconductor fabrication, ATMP/OSAT, electronic components and production-linked industrial policy.
stories.source_title: PIB, MeitY — Semicon 2.0 portal and ECMS approvals, 6 November 2026

stories.title: Centre doubles 2026–27 OMSS rice target and mandates weekly stock disclosure
stories.summary: The Department of Food and Public Distribution announced a package to improve rice availability and restrain prices. The Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) e-auction target for 2026–27 was doubled, and rice and paddy stocking entities were directed to update stocks weekly. The Centre also gave five southern states, including Tamil Nadu, concurrence to issue stock-limit control orders where necessary; this concurrence is not itself a statewide stock-limit order.
key_facts: The OMSS(D) rice sale target for 2026–27 rose from 25 lakh metric tonnes to 50 lakh metric tonnes.
Up to 31 October 2026, 25 LMT had been sold through e-auctions, compared with 11 LMT in the corresponding period of the previous year.
Traders, wholesalers, retailers, big-chain retailers and processors or millers must disclose rice and paddy stocks every Friday on the Food Stock Portal.
Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana may impose stock limits through appropriate control orders where considered necessary, up to 31 January 2027.
Additional Bharat Rice is to be allocated to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar, with emphasis on southern states.
stories.exam_link: Revise the Food Corporation of India, Open Market Sale Scheme, buffer stocks, Essential Commodities Act 1955, NAFED and NCCF.
stories.source_title: PIB, Department of Food and Public Distribution — OMSS rice and stock measures, 6 November 2026

stories.title: Startup India and I-STEM portals gain API integration for research-facility access
stories.summary: The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser and DPIIT launched API integration between Startup India and the Indian Science, Technology and Engineering Facilities Map. The integration helps DPIIT-recognised startups discover and request access to scientific, testing and prototyping facilities. It does not create an automatic right of access: host institutions will continue to decide requests based on suitability, availability, charges, safety and permissions.
key_facts: The integration enables automated verification of a startup's DPIIT recognition status.
Single Sign-On functionality is proposed for a subsequent phase, not reported as completed on launch day.
As of 6 November 2026, I-STEM listed 31,540 equipment items across 4,044 registered institutions.
I-STEM promotes shared use of publicly funded scientific infrastructure and can reduce duplication of expensive equipment.
stories.exam_link: Revise the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser, DPIIT, Startup India, research infrastructure sharing and the role of APIs in digital governance.
stories.source_title: PIB, Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser — Startup India–I-STEM API integration, 6 November 2026

stories.title: NHAI standardises infrastructure for barrier-free multi-lane tolling
stories.summary: NHAI issued guidelines for Multi-Lane Free Flow tolling infrastructure on four-lane and wider National Highways. The design framework covers layouts, lanes, gantries, lighting, signage and operational facilities so vehicles can be tolled without stopping at physical barriers. The guidelines apply to future and under-construction projects; they do not mean that all existing toll plazas became barrier-free on 6 November.
key_facts: Projects at the Detailed Project Report stage must incorporate the new design requirements.
Already awarded or under-construction projects are to adopt changes through applicable contractual provisions.
The guidelines provide for advance signs, lighting and electronic variable message signs to improve safety and user information.
Barrier-free tolling is intended to cut queues, waiting time and fuel use at toll plazas.
stories.exam_link: Revise NHAI, National Highways, FASTag, electronic toll collection, DPRs and the distinction between policy guidelines and nationwide implementation.
stories.source_title: PIB, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways — NHAI MLFF tolling guidelines, 6 November 2026

stories.title: TRAI digitises the register of interconnect agreements from 1 January 2027
stories.summary: TRAI released the Register of Interconnect Agreements (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026, which take effect on 1 January 2027. The amendment replaces legacy physical filing requirements with portal-based registration, searchable electronic documents and online access mechanisms. It also revises inspection and copy fees and introduces graded financial disincentives for contraventions.
key_facts: Agreements in force on 1 January 2027 must be submitted within 15 days from that date.
New agreements and modifications must be registered within 15 days of execution or modification.
Electronic copies must be supplied as text-searchable PDF documents.
The inspection fee is ₹1,500 per hour or part thereof, while copies or extracts cost ₹500 per page.
TRAI's authority to maintain the register is linked to Section 11(1)(b) of the TRAI Act 1997.
stories.exam_link: Revise TRAI as a statutory regulator, the TRAI Act 1997, telecom interconnection and the difference between regulations and executive guidelines.
stories.source_title: PIB, TRAI — Register of Interconnect Agreements Fourth Amendment Regulations, 6 November 2026

stories.title: NPPA reports price revisions before cancer-drug trade-margin cap takes effect
stories.summary: A PIB backgrounder reported implementation progress on NPPA's 17 October decision to cap trade margins on 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines at 30% of maximum retail price. By 4 November, 70 companies had reported revised MRPs for 120 drugs. The revised prices take effect on 9 November 2026, so the measure was not yet operational on the edition date.
key_facts: The list covers 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines, including patented medicines.
Reported MRP reductions average 20% to 70%, with the highest reported reduction at 96.45%.
The estimated saving stated by the government is ₹3,357.49 crore.
The cap was imposed under Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013.
Retailers, hospitals and medical institutions must charge the revised prices from 9 November and display applicable price lists.
stories.exam_link: Revise NPPA, scheduled and non-scheduled formulations, DPCO 2013, price control and the distinction between a trade-margin cap and a manufacturer price ceiling.
stories.source_title: PIB Backgrounder — Cancer-medicine trade-margin implementation update, 6 November 2026

stories.title: Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5 records nearly 40 lakh certificates in five days
stories.summary: The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare formally launched the nationwide Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5 and reported nearly 40 lakh certificates generated in its first five days. Face authentication accounted for nearly 80% of certificates during the period. Camps and doorstep services are intended to reduce the need for pensioners, especially those with mobility constraints, to visit banks or offices.
key_facts: The first five days produced nearly 40 lakh certificates, against about 25 lakh in the corresponding period a year earlier.
Face-authentication use rose from 61% to nearly 80% during the comparable period.
The campaign is planned across nearly 3,000 locations, with doorstep arrangements for pensioners unable to attend camps.
Banks, Railways, Defence, Posts, Telecommunications, MeitY, UIDAI, state governments and pensioners' associations participate in the whole-of-government campaign.
stories.exam_link: Revise Jeevan Pramaan, Aadhaar-based face authentication, digital delivery of pension services and the role of the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare.
stories.source_title: PIB, Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare — DLC Campaign 5 update, 6 November 2026

stories.title: VAJRA-SAT tabletop exercise tests preparedness for an unreported FMD serotype
stories.summary: The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying and ICAR-NIVEDI concluded the two-day VAJRA-SAT tabletop exercise in Bengaluru. It simulated preparedness for Foot-and-Mouth Disease serotype SAT-1, covering detection, laboratory confirmation, epidemiological investigation, movement control, vaccination readiness and inter-agency coordination. SAT-1 has not been reported in India; the exercise was preventive and not a response to a domestic outbreak.
key_facts: The exercise involved 83 participants from 25 states, three Union Territories and national institutions.
Its theme was 'Detect Early, Confirm Fast, Contain Together'.
SAT-1 has spread beyond Africa to parts of West Asia, motivating risk-based preparedness in India.
A separate discussion examined FMD-free compartmentalisation of semen production centres and semen banks.
stories.exam_link: Revise transboundary animal diseases, serotypes, ICAR-NIVEDI, disease surveillance, livestock movement controls and FMD-free compartmentalisation.
stories.source_title: PIB, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying — VAJRA-SAT exercise, 6 November 2026

mcqs.question: Which three Semicon 2.0 pillars opened for applications on 6 November 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Applications opened for Pillar 2 on machines and materials, Pillar 3 on more fabs and Pillar 4 on strengthening ATMP/OSAT.

mcqs.question: What is the approved fiscal outlay for Semicon 2.0?
mcqs.explanation: The Union Cabinet-approved outlay is ₹1,27,500 crore; the other figures relate to different investments or programme outcomes.

mcqs.question: The OMSS(D) rice e-auction target for 2026–27 was increased to what quantity?
mcqs.explanation: The target was doubled from 25 lakh metric tonnes to 50 lakh metric tonnes.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the Centre's 6 November rice stock-limit decision?
options: It automatically imposed one national stock limit
It allowed five southern states to issue control orders where necessary
It applied only to basmati exporters
mcqs.explanation: The Centre conveyed concurrence to five southern states, including Tamil Nadu, to impose limits through state control orders where considered necessary.

mcqs.question: What does the Startup India–I-STEM integration primarily help recognised startups do?
options: Discover and request access to research facilities
mcqs.explanation: The API integration helps startups discover equipment and request access; host institutions still evaluate each request.

mcqs.question: Which statement about I-STEM access after the API launch is correct?
options: Every request must be approved automatically
mcqs.explanation: Host institutions assess suitability, availability, charges, safety requirements and permissions before approving access.

mcqs.question: NHAI's new Multi-Lane Free Flow tolling design guidelines apply specifically to which roads?
mcqs.explanation: The guidelines standardise barrier-free tolling infrastructure for four-lane and above National Highways.

mcqs.question: When do TRAI's Fourth Amendment Regulations on the Register of Interconnect Agreements take effect?
mcqs.explanation: TRAI specified 1 January 2027 as the commencement date.

mcqs.question: Under the amended TRAI framework, in what format must interconnect agreements be submitted electronically?
mcqs.explanation: The regulations require text-searchable PDF documents to support processing, maintenance and retrieval.

mcqs.question: NPPA capped trade margins on the identified non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines at what percentage of MRP?
mcqs.explanation: The trade-margin cap is 30% of maximum retail price for the 137 identified medicines.

mcqs.question: On what date were the revised cancer-medicine prices scheduled to take effect?
mcqs.explanation: The revision was reported before implementation; the effective date is 9 November 2026.

mcqs.question: What authentication method accounted for nearly 80% of Digital Life Certificates in the first five days of Campaign 5?
mcqs.explanation: The campaign reported that face authentication rose to nearly 80% of certificates generated in the period.

mcqs.question: VAJRA-SAT was a preparedness exercise for which disease?
mcqs.explanation: VAJRA-SAT simulated preparedness for Foot-and-Mouth Disease serotype SAT-1.

mcqs.question: Which fact about FMD serotype SAT-1 was central to the VAJRA-SAT exercise?
options: It is endemic in every Indian state
It has not been reported in India
mcqs.explanation: SAT-1 has not been reported in India; the tabletop exercise was a proactive preparedness measure, not an outbreak response.
